Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Timothy Bentum announces five-year anti-drug tour targeting 252 SHSs across Ghana Source : Emmanuel Tetteh 17 November 2026 11:39am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Media personality and Lead Pastor of Grace Avenue Ministry, Timothy Bentum, has announced a five-year anti-drug abuse campaign targeting 252 senior high schools across Ghana's 16 regions to educate students on substance abuse, peer pressure and the dangers of addiction.
The initiative, which will involve sustained engagements with students and teachers, is aimed at preventing young people from experimenting with drugs and helping those already facing challenges to access counselling and support.
Mr Bentum said the campaign would focus particularly on peer influence, noting that many people who develop drug-related problems are first introduced to substances by friends.
He said schools provided an important platform for addressing the problem because they brought young people and their friends together, making them suitable environments for conversations about responsible friendships and the consequences of peer pressure.
He urged students to be careful about the company they keep, warning that the desire to improve academic performance or gain confidence must not drive them towards substance abuse.
"There is no drug that can make you study better or give you confidence without the clap back of getting addicted and then totally throwing away your whole destiny," he cautioned.
Mr Bentum stressed that the campaign would not be a one-off awareness exercise but a sustained intervention spanning five years and covering all 16 regions.
As part of the programme, organisers intend to identify three to four teachers in each participating school and equip them with basic counselling skills to support students experiencing personal difficulties.
The selected teachers will serve as the first point of contact for students who need guidance, emotional support or someone to talk to, helping to create a more accessible support system within schools.
He also appealed to parents to become more actively involved in their children's lives, stressing that their responsibilities must go beyond providing financial support.
"I want every parent out there to be more present in their children's lives beyond just trying to support with money. I really want the biggest support you can give as a nation and as individuals is to be part of your children's lives," he said.
He called for collective support from parents, individuals and society to protect young people from substance abuse and its long-term consequences.
The anti-drug high school tour will be officially launched on Saturday, November 21, at 3:00 p.m. at Christ the King Church in Accra.
